docs.title: taken
docs.text:
"A very particular set of skills, acquired over a very long career."

taken is a personal dotfile-style CLI for managing AI agent skills (SKILL.md files). Think chezmoi, but for agent skills — your skills live in ~/.taken/, are git-backed, and can be linked into any project on demand.

Fully compatible with the skills.sh ecosystem (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, and 40+ agents).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv tool install taken-cli

pipx install taken-cli

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Initialize 

taken init
Sets up ~/.taken/, prompts for your namespace, creates config and registry.

2. Create a personal skill 

taken add my-skill
Scaffolds ~/.taken/skills/<you>/my-skill/SKILL.md and opens it in your editor.

3. Adopt an existing skill from a project 

taken add ./agents/my-skill/
Copies the skill folder into ~/.taken/ and registers it, detecting provenance from skills.sh lock files automatically.

4. Install a skill from GitHub 

taken install vercel-labs/agent-skills
taken install vercel-labs/agent-skills/react-best-practices
Interactive fuzzy picker when multiple skills are found.

5. Use a skill in a project 

taken use
Fuzzy-picks from your registry and copies the skill into .agents/skills/ in the current project.

6. Push edits back to registry 

taken save
Promotes refined project skills back to ~/.taken/ so they propagate to future projects.

7. Update project skills 

taken update
Re-copies the latest registry version into the project.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description GITHUB_TOKEN GitHub personal access token. Set this to avoid API rate limits when using taken install or taken update. TAKEN_HOME Override the default ~/.taken/ location. Useful for testing or keeping multiple isolated taken environments. VISUAL / EDITOR Editor opened by taken add when scaffolding a new skill. Falls back to vim if neither is set.

docs.title: config.yaml
docs.text:
~/.taken/config.yaml is written by taken init and read on every command. It is not currently editable via CLI — edit it directly if needed.

Key Description username Your skill namespace (set during taken init). initialized_at ISO 8601 timestamp of last initialization. auto_commit If true, taken commits to ~/.taken/ automatically after mutating commands. Not yet CLI-exposed — defaults to true. auto_push If true, taken pushes after each auto-commit. Not yet CLI-exposed — defaults to false.

docs.title: taken add
docs.text: Create a new personal skill or adopt an existing skill folder into taken management.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
taken add <skill-name>       # create a new skill
taken add <path/to/folder>   # adopt an existing skill folder

docs.title: Create mode
docs.text:
When you pass a plain name, taken scaffolds a new skill under your namespace and opens it in your editor.

taken add my-skill

What happens:

  1. Creates ~/.taken/skills/<username>/my-skill/SKILL.md
  2. Registers it as a personal skill
  3. Opens SKILL.md in your $VISUAL / $EDITOR (falls back to vim)

Name rules: lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores only. Must start with a letter or number. Do not include a namespace — your username is added automatically.

taken add react-best-practices   # ✓
taken add you/react-practices    # ✗ — namespace not allowed here
taken add my skill               # ✗ — no spaces

docs.title: Adopt mode
docs.text:
When you pass a path (absolute or relative, must point to a directory), taken copies it into ~/.taken/ and registers it.

taken add ./agents/my-skill/
taken add /path/to/skill-folder/

Taken detects the argument as a path if it starts with /, ./, or ../.

Provenance detection: if a skills.sh lock file (.agents/skills.lock) exists in the current project, taken reads it to determine the original source, namespace, and version of the skill automatically. Without a lock file, the skill is registered as personal under your namespace.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• If the skill already exists in your registry, the command exits with an error.
  • After adoption or creation, a git commit is made in ~/.taken/ automatically (if auto_commit is enabled).

docs.title: taken git
docs.text: Run any git command inside ~/.taken/.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: taken git <git args>

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A thin passthrough to git with ~/.taken/ as the working directory. Any valid git subcommand works.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
taken git status
taken git log --oneline
taken git remote add origin git@github.com:you/taken-skills.git
taken git push -u origin main
taken git pull

This is the recommended way to push your ~/.taken/ repository to a remote for backup or sharing across machines.

docs.title: taken init
docs.text: First-time setup for taken. Creates ~/.taken/, prompts for your skill namespace, and initializes a git repository.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
taken init

No arguments or flags.

docs.title: Username selection
docs.text:
taken needs a namespace to store your personal skills under (~/.taken/skills/<username>/). On first run it offers three choices:

  1. System username — the result of whoami (always available)
  2. Git config name — pulled from git config user.name (shown only if set)
  3. Enter manually — free-text prompt for any name you prefer

The default is option 1. Press Enter to accept it or pick another option.

docs.title: What gets created
docs.text:
After you choose a username, taken init creates:

Path Description ~/.taken/skills/<username>/ Your personal skill namespace directory ~/.taken/config.yaml Config file with your username and initialization timestamp ~/.taken/registry.yaml Empty skill registry (source of truth for all managed skills) ~/.taken/.git/ Git repository with an initial commit

docs.title: Reinitializing
docs.text:
Running taken init when ~/.taken/ already exists triggers a reinitialization flow.

taken will ask whether you want to proceed, then offer two reset modes:

Mode What it does Reset config only (default) Overwrites config.yaml with new username/timestamp. Skills and registry are preserved. Full wipe Deletes ~/.taken/ entirely, then reinitializes from scratch. Requires a second confirmation.

Warning

Full wipe is irreversible if you have not pushed your ~/.taken/ git repository to a remote.

docs.title: taken install
docs.text: Install one or more skills from a GitHub repository.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: taken install <source> [options]

docs.title: Source formats
docs.text:
taken install vercel-labs/agent-skills                       # all skills (interactive picker)
taken install vercel-labs/agent-skills/react-best-practices  # specific skill by path
taken install https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills    # full URL

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Flag Description --skill <name> Install a specific skill by name (repeatable). Skips the interactive picker. --ref <branch\|tag\|sha> Install from a specific branch, tag, or commit SHA. Defaults to the repo's default branch. --pin Lock to the exact commit SHA — taken update will never auto-upgrade this skill.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Resolves the ref to a commit SHA
  2. Discovers all SKILL.md files in the repository
  3. If multiple skills are found and no --skill filter is given, shows a fuzzy picker (space/tab to select, enter to confirm)
  4. Downloads and registers each selected skill under ~/.taken/skills/<owner>/<skill-name>/

Already-registered skills are skipped without error.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Install a single specific skill non-interactively
taken install vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill react-best-practices

# Install multiple skills at once
taken install vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill react-best-practices --skill typescript

# Install from a specific tag and pin it
taken install vercel-labs/agent-skills --ref v1.2.0 --pin

docs.title: GitHub rate limits
docs.text:
Unauthenticated requests are limited to 60/hour. Set GITHUB_TOKEN to avoid hitting limits:

export GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_...

docs.title: taken list
docs.text: Show all skills in your registry.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: taken list

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Displays a table with four columns:

Column Description Skill Full name in namespace/skill-name format Source How the skill was added — personal, npx, or taken Version First 8 characters of the commit SHA (for installed skills), or 1 for personal skills Date Creation date (personal) or install date (installed)

A count of total skills is shown below the table.

docs.title: Source types
docs.text: Source Meaning personal Created with taken add or adopted from a local path without a lock file npx Adopted from a project that used the skills.sh npx installer taken Installed from GitHub via taken install

docs.title: taken remove
docs.text: Remove a skill from your registry and delete its files from ~/.taken/.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
taken remove                     # interactive fuzzy picker
taken remove <namespace/skill>   # direct, non-interactive

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
For each selected skill, taken asks for confirmation before removing:

Remove namespace/my-skill? [y/N]

On confirmation:

  1. Deletes ~/.taken/skills/<namespace>/<skill-name>/
  2. Removes the entry from registry.yaml
  3. Commits the change to ~/.taken/

Project copies are not affected. Skills already copied into .agents/skills/ in your projects remain untouched — taken remove only affects the registry.

Warning

This is irreversible unless you have pushed ~/.taken/ to a remote and can restore from there. For GitHub-installed skills, you can always reinstall with taken install.

docs.title: taken save
docs.text: Push project skill edits back to your ~/.taken/ registry.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
taken save                       # interactive fuzzy picker
taken save <namespace/skill>     # direct, non-interactive

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
taken save is the reverse of taken use. After refining a skill while working in a project, use this command to promote those edits back to the registry so they propagate to future projects.

For each selected skill:

  • If the file hash matches what was originally copied — reported as "no changes", nothing written
  • If the hash differs — the project copy is copied back to ~/.taken/skills/<ns>/<name>/, the registry and .taken.yaml are updated, and a git commit is made in ~/.taken/

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Must be run from a directory containing .taken.yaml (i.e., a project where taken use was previously run)
  • The skill must be tracked in that .taken.yaml

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# Edit a skill in the project
vim .agents/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md

# Push the edit back to registry
taken save my-namespace/my-skill
# ✓ my-namespace/my-skill → ~/.taken/skills/my-namespace/my-skill/

docs.title: taken update
docs.text: Re-copy the latest registry version of a skill into the current project.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
taken update                     # interactive fuzzy picker
taken update <namespace/skill>   # direct, non-interactive

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
For each selected skill, taken compares the current project copy against the registry version using file hashes and takes one of these paths:

State Action Registry and project both unchanged Reported as "already up to date" Registry changed, project unchanged Copies registry version into project Registry unchanged, project has local edits Suggests taken save — no overwrite Registry changed, project also has local edits Prompts before overwriting

docs.title: GitHub refresh (floating skills)
docs.text:
For skills installed via taken install that are not pinned, taken update first checks GitHub for upstream changes before copying to the project:

  1. Fetches the latest commit SHA from the default branch
  2. Compares the upstream skill folder hash to the registry copy
  3. Re-downloads the skill if the upstream version has changed
  4. Then re-copies the (now updated) registry version into the project

Pinned skills (installed with --pin) are never auto-upgraded.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Must be run from a directory containing .taken.yaml.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
taken update vercel-labs/react-best-practices
# ↑ vercel-labs/react-best-practices abc123 → def456  (refreshed from GitHub)
# ✓ vercel-labs/react-best-practices → .agents/skills/react-best-practices/

docs.title: taken use
docs.text: Copy a skill from your registry into the current project.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
taken use                        # interactive fuzzy picker
taken use <namespace/skill>      # direct, non-interactive

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. If no argument is given, shows a fuzzy picker over your full registry (space/tab to select multiple, enter to confirm)
  2. Copies the skill folder into .agents/skills/<skill-name>/ in the current working directory
  3. Records the copy in .taken.yaml at the project root (created if it doesn't exist)

.taken.yaml is meant to be committed — it lets teammates use the skills without needing taken installed.

docs.title: Overwrite protection
docs.text:
If a skill already exists in the project and you've modified it locally, taken detects the change by comparing file hashes and prompts before overwriting:

⚠  my-skill has local changes in your project.
  Overwrite my-skill? [y/N]

Decline to keep your local edits. Use taken save to push them back to the registry first.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
cd my-project
taken use
# → fuzzy picker → select react-best-practices, typescript
# → copies to .agents/skills/react-best-practices/ and .agents/skills/typescript/
# → updates .taken.yaml
